chapter: Bolden and the road to New Orleans
title: Last time Ory saw Bolden
summary: Ory recalls Bolden at Masonic Hall spending the money and rumors of his later madness.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Last time I saw Bowlin, King Bowlin, I saw him at Masonic Hall. And he had a little trouble. I would stay there until the dance was over on a Monday night. And they shot... They'd spent all the deposit he'd receive on engagement. And when they paid him the rest, he'd had enough money to finish paying the boys, you know. So he started issuing it out. He said, yeah, it was your Colorado boys. He looked at that and he had 60 cents left. He said, this is for Chucky. No one gonna get this for Chucky. And he's Chucky. And he walked away.
Yeah. What does that mean? His wife.
That's the last time you saw him, huh? Yeah.
Next time he heard of him, he'd gone crazy. Yeah, he was in Jackson, Mississippi. Yeah.
Oh, he lived for years afterwards. He claimed the poison, I don't know. He put something on his mouthpiece.
Yeah. Oh, really? Is that what he said?
Some of the women... Oh, no. Oh, that's what the people said. Yeah, they run through the grapevine, you know. Yes. Oh, but he had lots of women.
